title: Microstall trigger investigation and fairness reconciliation playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: SUMMARY: During a capacity spike on 2026-02-28 (INC-2026-07) we observed repeated ~200ms microstalls in batch formation causing 99th percentile token latency to spike by ~3x for interactive chat workloads. The incidents show coupling between small aggressive scheduling windows, KV-cache warmup behavior, and priority preemption that produced unfair slot starvation for low-weight requests. This ticket consolidates the investigation notes and defines a playbook to detect, mitigate, and reconcile fairness regressions.
steps_taken: 2026-02-28 10:12: triage: paged on-call, collected heap/queue metrics and slow-path traces
2026-02-28 10:40: rolled hotfix: increase slot-alloc timeout from 5ms to 15ms in canary to reduce microstall sensitivity
2026-03-01 09:00: instrumented continuous-batcher with slot-acquisition histograms and per-priority backlog counters
2026-03-03 14:30: ran targeted loadtests reproducing stall pattern using chat-sim v2 with weighted priority mix
2026-03-05 16:20: merged KV-cache prefetch guard to avoid race between prefetch and batch-coalescer start (PR #7841)
2026-03-10 11:00: deployed metrics alert for repeated short-duration gaps (>=3 gaps in 1s) to staging
findings: Microstall root causes are multi-factor: short wall-clock batch windows (<=8ms) interact poorly with GC pauses and kernel scheduling jitter on noisy hosts
Priority preemption implemented in nov-2025 change reduces long-tail for P0 but increases slot churn for lower priorities leading to starvation bursts
KV-cache prefetch can delay first-token emission by taking a lock that blocks coalescer tick when timed with slot assignment
Batcher backoff logic lacked hysteresis: after a short stall the system aggressively reduces window, causing a cascade of tiny windows and repeated stalls
Incidents cluster on hosts with high interrupt load (ephemeral system-level noise) — correlation with noisy-host metric is high (Pearson r=0.63)
Existing dashboards surface per-route latency but not per-priority batch-formation success rate, making detection late
action_items: A1: Implement slot-acquisition circuit breaker that forces a fallback to larger-window coalescing when >3 microstalls occur within 5s (owner: Luca, estimate 3)
A2: Add hysteresis to window shrink/grow algorithm: require sustained improvement for 50ms before shrinking window (owner: Priya Rao, estimate 2)
A3: Decouple KV-cache prefetch lock from coalescer tick path; convert to try-lock with bounded delay and async completion fallback (owner: Mateo, estimate 5, depends_on ENG-99500)
A4: Expose per-priority batch-formation metrics (success_rate, average_wait_ms) in Console and add alert (owner: Observability Team, estimate 3)
A5: Add noisy-host tagging and auto-eviction policy for hosts exceeding interrupt/steal thresholds during heavy load (owner: Infra, estimate 4)
A6: Run a 2-week canary with staggered window configs (A/B/C) across traffic slices and collect fairness signals using existing eval harness (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-31)
A7: Update runbook: include diagnostic query for 'microstall gap pattern' and remediation commands to bump slot-alloc timeout and revert priority preemption per-route (owner: Oncall Docs, estimate 1)
A8: Postmortem follow-up: schedule a cross-team review for runtime-2.3 and prioritize backfill for affected customers (owner: Asha, due 2026-03-18)
A9: Add workload-weighted fairness test to CI that simulates skewed low-priority dominated traffic and asserts <10% request-redistribution after 5 minutes (owner: Testinfra, estimate 3)
